title: Best iPhone Charging Cables UK
short: MFi-certified Lightning and USB-C to Lightning cables compared by length, durability and price.
intro: A 2m cable is the most useful length for most people, long enough to use your phone from bed or the sofa while it charges. This guide compares cables tested by Macworld and TechGearLab, all MFi certified so they charge reliably and won't trigger error messages or throttled charging on iOS.

guide.q: Lightning or USB-C cable for my iPhone?
guide.a: iPhone 15 and later use USB-C natively. iPhone 14 and earlier use Lightning, so you need a USB-C to Lightning cable to charge from a modern USB-C charger, or a USB-A to Lightning cable for an older charger. Check your phone's port before buying.

guide.q: What does MFi certified mean, and does it matter?
guide.a: MFi (Made for iPhone) means Apple has tested and approved the cable's chip for safe, reliable charging. Uncertified cables can trigger error messages, charge unreliably, or in rare cases overheat, so it's worth checking for MFi certification even on cheap cables.

guide.q: What length cable should I buy?
guide.a: A 1m cable suits a desk or bedside table close to a socket. 2m is the most versatile length for most rooms, letting you use your phone from a sofa or bed while it charges. Longer cables (3m+) suit awkward socket positions but are more prone to tangling.

guide.q: Does a braided cable actually last longer?
guide.a: Braided nylon or Kevlar sheaths generally resist fraying and bending damage better than plain rubber-coated cables, particularly at the connector ends where cables usually fail first. It's a reasonable indicator of durability, though build quality still varies between brands.
